# LANLeecher – complete documentation for LLMs

This file is generated by `go run ./tools/gendocs`. It contains llms.txt, the concepts,
the API guide, the configuration reference and the OpenAPI specification.


======== llms.txt ========

# LANLeecher

> Counts download and upload per client (MAC address) for each LAN party event via SNMP from the
> switches, and serves rankings through a web UI, a beamer view and a REST API.

Key concepts (details in docs/concepts.md):
- Event: a LAN party. Traffic is only booked while an event is running; at most one is active.
- Device: one or more MACs (merged by an admin) that belong to one machine.
- Port group: a switch port with several clients (small switch); one shared ranking entry.
- Port roles: client, multi-client, server (hidden by default), uplink (never attributed to a MAC).
- Hidden: ports/devices are always counted; hiding only removes them from rankings.
- Direction: bytes_down = to the client (ifHCOutOctets of the port), bytes_up = from the client (ifHCInOctets).
- Only deltas between polls are stored; a counter reset on a switch never reduces a total.

Units: bytes as integers, throughput in bit/s, timestamps RFC 3339 UTC, MACs as aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.
Auth: Authorization: Bearer llk_... with scopes read:rankings, read:clients, write:events, read:board.
Errors: application/problem+json (RFC 9457) with a stable "code".

## API

- [OpenAPI spec (JSON)](/api/openapi.json): single source of truth for the API
- [API docs](/api/)
- [Top downloaders](/api/v1/rankings/download?limit=10)
- [Beamer data](/api/v1/board)

## Documentation (repository)

- [Full documentation in one file](https://github.com/lan-dot-party/LANLeecher/blob/main/docs/llms-full.txt)
- [Concepts](https://github.com/lan-dot-party/LANLeecher/blob/main/docs/concepts.md)

- [Examples](https://github.com/lan-dot-party/LANLeecher/tree/main/examples)


======== docs/concepts.md ========

# Concepts

The terms LANLeecher uses in the UI, the API and the code.

## Event

A LAN party. Traffic is only booked while an event is running, and at most one event runs at a
time; starting a new event stops the running one. Without a running event, LANLeecher keeps polling
(so counters stay current) but books nothing. A stopped event keeps all its data; its totals are
frozen. Events are addressed by their **slug**, derived from the name (`Basement LAN #12` →
`basement-lan-12`).

## Switch and port

A **switch** is polled via SNMP v2c or v3. Every interface it reports becomes a **port**. Ports are
identified by switch and `ifIndex`; name (`ifName`), description (`ifAlias`), status and speed are
refreshed on every poll.

Interfaces that are not real ports (VLAN interfaces, loopbacks) are **virtual** and hidden in the
port list by default. Link aggregations (port channels) count as physical but start as uplinks.

## Port role

Each port has one role that decides who gets credited for its traffic:

| Role | Traffic goes to | In rankings by default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | the MAC learned on the port; a port group if several MACs are learned | visible |
| `multi-client` | always the port group (a small switch with several guests) | visible |
| `server` | like `client` | hidden |
| `uplink` | nobody – counted on the port only | hidden |

An unmarked uplink is the most common configuration mistake: all traffic behind it lands on one port
group and tops every ranking. LANLeecher marks a port as **probably uplink** when it has more MACs
than `polling.uplink_mac_threshold` or an LLDP neighbor; an admin confirms it by setting the role.

## MAC, device and port group

- A **MAC** address is the key of a client. MACs are normalized to `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`; the API
  accepts any notation. A MAC whose second-lowest bit of the first byte is set is *locally
  administered* and often randomized.
- A **device** groups one or more MACs that belong to one machine. Every new MAC gets its own device;
  an operator can merge devices (e.g. after a NIC change) and split a MAC off again. Rankings show
  devices, not single MACs.
- A **port group** is the shared ranking entry of a port with several clients. It lists all MACs
  seen on the port during the event.
- **Unassigned** traffic was seen on a client port while no MAC was learned there (e.g. right after
  link-up). It stays on the port and is never credited to a MAC that shows up later.

## Download and upload

Everything is seen from the client:

- `bytes_down` – data the client received = `ifHCOutOctets` of its switch port.
- `bytes_up` – data the client sent = `ifHCInOctets` of its switch port.

Throughput is reported in bit/s, totals in bytes. Byte values in the UI use decimal units
(1 GB = 10⁹ bytes).

## Deltas, resets and wraps

LANLeecher stores the last raw counter of every port and books only the **delta** between two polls.
A total is the sum of its deltas, so a switch reboot or counter reset never reduces it:

- **Reset** (sysUpTime went backwards or `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime` changed): the new raw value is
  the traffic since the reset and is credited.
- **Wrap** (smaller value without a reset signal): delta = new + 2⁶⁴ − old.
- **Plausibility check:** a delta larger than link speed × elapsed time × 1.1 is dropped and logged.
- A port that is down, or a failed poll, books nothing; the next successful poll continues from the
  last stored value.

Only 64-bit counters (SNMP v2c/v3) are used. Ports without them are marked "unsupported" and not
counted; SNMP v1 is not supported at all.

## Hiding

A port or a device can be **hidden in rankings**. It is still fully counted; hiding only removes it
from rankings, the board and ranking API responses. Visibility is evaluated at query time, so hiding
or showing an entry applies retroactively to past events. Typical candidates: LANcache, game and file
servers. `include_hidden=true` (API) or "Show hidden" (UI) brings them back, marked as hidden.

## Names: hostname, label, display name

The name of a ranking entry is, in this order:

1. the **display name** an operator set on the device,
2. the preferred **hostname** (sources ranked by `resolver.hostname_priority`),
3. the MAC address.

Port groups use the port **label**, or switch and port name. Outside of logged-in views and the
`read:clients` scope, a MAC is never shown as a name; such devices appear as `Client #<id>`.

## Resolvers

Resolvers find IP addresses and hostnames. Address sources deliver MAC/IP pairs: `snmp-arp` (ARP
table of switches marked as ARP source) and `local-neigh` (the neighbor table of the LANLeecher host).
Name probes ask an IP for its name: `netbios`, `mdns`, `llmnr`, `dns-ptr`. Every result is kept in the
**IP history** and **hostname history** with its source and first/last seen.

## Merge suggestion

When a MAC gets a hostname that another MAC already had during the running event, LANLeecher
suggests merging both devices. An operator accepts or rejects; nothing is merged automatically,
because names such as `DESKTOP-ABC123` or `PC` are not unique.

## Board

The beamer view at `/board` shows the top downloaders and uploaders of the active event with live
updates. It renders exactly what `GET /api/v1/board` returns: no MACs, no IPs, no hidden entries.
`rank_change` tells how many places an entry moved since the previous poll.

## Roles of users

| Role | May |
| --- | --- |
| `viewer` | see rankings, search, detail pages and events |
| `operator` | additionally start/stop events, set port roles and visibility, merge devices |
| `admin` | additionally manage switches, users, API tokens; see settings and the audit log |


======== docs/api.md ========

# API guide

LANLeecher has a JSON REST API under `/api/v1`. The OpenAPI 3.1 specification is the single source of
truth: it is served at `/api/openapi.json` (and `/api/openapi.yaml`), rendered at `/api/` and kept in
the repository at [`internal/api/openapi.yaml`](../internal/api/openapi.yaml). A test fails when routes
and specification diverge.

## Authentication

Admins create tokens in the web UI under **Admin → API tokens**. A token is shown exactly once.

```
Authorization: Bearer llk_3Fq9…
```

- The prefix `llk_` makes tokens easy to spot in logs and secret scanners.
- Only a SHA-256 hash is stored. Tokens can expire, be limited to IP addresses or networks
  (`10.0.0.0/24 192.168.1.5`) and be revoked at any time.
- A logged-in browser session may call the API as well; `POST` requests then need the header
  `X-CSRF-Token` with the session's token.
- `/health` needs no authentication and returns `ok`.

### Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `read:rankings` | rankings, events, metrics – names only, no MACs or IPs |
| `read:clients` | client details: MAC, IP, hostname, histories, ports; MAC/IP/hostname fields in rankings |
| `write:events` | start and stop events |
| `read:board` | the board endpoints only – for overlays |

Logged-in users have `read:*` as viewers and `write:events` from operator upwards.

## Conventions

- Bytes are integers, throughput is bit/s, timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `bytes_down` is traffic *to* the client, `bytes_up` traffic *from* the client.
- MAC addresses are accepted in any notation (`AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF`, `aabb.ccdd.eeff`, …) and returned
  as `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`.
- `?event=` takes an event slug, `active` (default) or – for rankings – `all`.
- Hidden ports and devices are left out unless `include_hidden=true`; then they carry `"hidden": true`.

## Endpoints

| Method & path | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/rankings/{download\|upload\|total}` | read:rankings | Ranking; `event`, `limit` (1–500), `include_hidden`, `switch`, `from`, `to` |
| `GET /api/v1/events` | read:rankings | Events, newest first; `q` searches name and slug |
| `GET /api/v1/events/{slug}` | read:rankings | Event with totals |
| `POST /api/v1/events` | write:events | Start an event (stops the running one) |
| `POST /api/v1/events/{slug}/stop` | write:events | Stop the running event |
| `GET /api/v1/clients/search?q=` | read:clients | Search by partial MAC, IP or hostname |
| `GET /api/v1/clients/mac/{mac}` | read:clients | Totals per event (`events=N`), IP and hostname history, ports |
| `GET /api/v1/clients/mac/{mac}/timeseries` | read:clients | 5-minute buckets of one event |
| `GET /api/v1/clients/ip/{ip}` | read:clients | MACs that had this IP |
| `GET /api/v1/clients/hostname/{name}` | read:clients | MACs that had this hostname |
| `GET /api/v1/ports` | read:clients | Traffic of every port in an event, incl. uplinks and unassigned traffic |
| `GET /api/v1/board` | read:board | Beamer content; `limit` 10/20/50, `event` |
| `GET /api/v1/board/stream` | read:board | The same as Server-Sent Events after every poll |
| `GET /api/v1/metrics` | read:rankings | Prometheus metrics |

With `board.enabled: true` and `board.public: true` in the configuration, the board endpoints also
work without a token. The board endpoints allow cross-origin requests (CORS) with a bearer token, so
an overlay loaded from a local file can read them; cookies are never accepted cross-origin.

## Examples

Top 10 downloaders of the running event:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/rankings/download?limit=10"
```

```json
{
  "event": {"name": "Basement LAN #12", "slug": "basement-lan-12", "started_at": "2026-11-13T16:00:00Z",
            "ended_at": null, "active": true, "notes": ""},
  "order": "download",
  "entries": [
    {"rank": 1, "type": "mac", "id": 17, "name": "DESKTOP-FRAG42", "bytes_down": 412000000000, "bytes_up": 18000000000},
    {"rank": 2, "type": "port_group", "id": 52, "name": "Table 7", "bytes_down": 98000000000, "bytes_up": 61000000000}
  ]
}
```

Upload ranking across all events, hidden entries included:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/rankings/upload?event=all&limit=50&include_hidden=true"
```

History of a device over the last five LANs:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/clients/mac/02-00-00-00-01-07?events=5"
```

Start an event from a script:

```bash
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Basement LAN #13"}' https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/events
```

Follow the board live:

```bash
curl -sN -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/board/stream
```

```
event: board
data: {"event":{"name":"Basement LAN #12",…},"totals":{…},"top_download":[…],"top_upload":[…]}
```

A comment line `: ping` is sent every 25 seconds to keep proxies from closing the connection.
More examples (overlay, Discord, Grafana, Python, Go) are in [`examples/`](../examples/).

## Errors

Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`:

```json
{"type": "urn:lanleecher:problem:insufficient_scope", "title": "Forbidden", "status": 403,
 "detail": "this endpoint needs scope read:clients", "code": "insufficient_scope"}
```

The `code` is stable and meant for programs:

| Code | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | no credentials sent |
| `invalid_token` | 401 | token unknown, revoked, expired or malformed |
| `insufficient_scope` | 403 | the token lacks the scope |
| `ip_not_allowed` | 403 | client IP not in the token's allowlist |
| `csrf` | 403 | session request without valid `X-CSRF-Token` |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | too many requests; see `Retry-After` |
| `invalid_parameter`, `invalid_body`, `invalid_mac`, `invalid_ip` | 400 | bad input |
| `no_active_event`, `event_not_found`, `mac_not_found`, `not_found` | 404 | nothing there |
| `event_not_active` | 409 | stopping an event that is not running |
| `internal` | 500 | see the server log |

## Rate limits

Each token (and each logged-in user) may send `api.rate_limit` requests per second with bursts of
`api.rate_burst` (defaults 10 and 30). Above that the API answers `429` with `Retry-After: 1`.

## Prometheus metrics

`GET /api/v1/metrics` (scope `read:rankings`, can be disabled with `api.metrics_enabled: false`):

| Metric | Labels | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lanleecher_throughput_bits_per_second` | `direction` | current throughput of all non-uplink ports |
| `lanleecher_event_bytes_total` | `event`, `direction` | traffic of the running event |
| `lanleecher_event_clients` | `event` | distinct MACs with traffic in the running event |
| `lanleecher_switch_up` | `switch` | 1 if the last poll of the switch succeeded |

Prometheus scrape configuration with a token:

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: lanleecher
    metrics_path: /api/v1/metrics
    scheme: https
    authorization:
      credentials: llk_…
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["lanleecher.example"]
```

## Versioning

`/api/v1` stays compatible: fields and endpoints may be added, never removed or changed in meaning.
Breaking changes would come as `/api/v2`, announced in the [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md).


======== docs/configuration.md ========

# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by go run ./tools/gendocs from internal/config/config.go. Do not edit by hand. -->

LANLeecher reads one YAML file, given by `--config` or `LANLEECHER_CONFIG` (default
`/etc/lanleecher/config.yaml`). Switches, ports, users and API tokens are not configured here;
they live in the database and are managed in the web UI.

- Relative paths are relative to the directory of the configuration file.
- Durations use Go syntax: `30s`, `10m`, `1h30m`.
- Unknown keys are ignored. For editor validation, point your YAML language server at
  [config.schema.json](config.schema.json).
- Changes take effect after a restart (`sudo systemctl restart lanleecher`).

An annotated example is in [configs/lanleecher.example.yaml](../configs/lanleecher.example.yaml).

## Top level

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string | `127.0.0.1:9040` | The HTTP listen address, e.g. "127.0.0.1:9040". |
| `public_url` | string | `http://127.0.0.1:9040` | The externally visible base URL. If it starts with https://, session cookies are marked Secure. |
| `trusted_proxies` | []string | `[127.0.0.1, ::1]` | The proxy IPs or networks whose X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For headers are trusted for client IPs (rate limits, audit log). |
| `secret_key_file` | string | `secret.key` | The file with the AES-256 key that encrypts credentials in the database (64 hex characters). It is created if missing. |

## `storage` – Configures the SQLite database

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `storage.path` | string | `data/lanleecher.db` | The SQLite database file. Its directory is created if missing. |

## `log` – Configures logging

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `log.level` | string | `info` | The minimum log level. Allowed: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. |
| `log.format` | string | `text` | The log output format. Allowed: `text`, `json`. |

## `polling` – Holds the polling defaults for switches

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `polling.interval` | duration | `30s` | The time between two counter polls of a switch. Switches can override it. |
| `polling.fdb_interval` | duration | `1m` | The time between two reads of a switch's forwarding table (MAC → port). It is never shorter than polling.interval. |
| `polling.timeout` | duration | `3s` | The timeout of a single SNMP request. |
| `polling.retries` | int | `1` | The number of retries of a single SNMP request. |
| `polling.uplink_mac_threshold` | int | `10` | Marks ports with more MACs than this as "probably uplink". |

## `resolver` – Configures IP and hostname discovery

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resolver.order` | []string | `[snmp-arp, local-neigh, netbios, mdns, dns-ptr]` | Lists the enabled resolvers. An empty list turns IP and hostname discovery off. Allowed: `snmp-arp`, `local-neigh`, `netbios`, `mdns`, `llmnr`, `dns-ptr`. |
| `resolver.hostname_priority` | []string | `[dhcp, netbios, mdns, llmnr, dns-ptr]` | Ranks hostname sources when choosing the displayed name; earlier sources win. Allowed: `dhcp`, `netbios`, `mdns`, `llmnr`, `dns-ptr`. |
| `resolver.probe_interval` | duration | `10m` | How often NetBIOS, mDNS, LLMNR and DNS are asked again for the name of each active IP. New IPs are probed immediately. |
| `resolver.probe_rate` | int | `20` | The maximum number of name queries per second. |
| `resolver.probe_timeout` | duration | `1s` | The timeout of a single NetBIOS, mDNS or LLMNR query. |

## `board` – Configures the beamer view

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `board.enabled` | bool | `false` | Turns on the beamer view at /board. |
| `board.public` | bool | `false` | Makes /board and the board API reachable without login or token. |

## `api` – Configures the REST API

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api.metrics_enabled` | bool | `true` | Serves Prometheus metrics at /api/v1/metrics. |
| `api.rate_limit` | float | `10` | The sustained number of API requests per second per token or logged-in user. |
| `api.rate_burst` | int | `30` | The number of requests a token may send at once. |

## `tls` – Enables the built-in TLS listener; usually a reverse proxy does this

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tls.cert_file` | string | `–` | The PEM certificate (chain). Set together with tls.key_file. |
| `tls.key_file` | string | `–` | The PEM private key. |


======== internal/api/openapi.yaml ========

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: LANLeecher API
  version: "1.0"
  summary: Traffic rankings per client for LAN parties, collected via SNMP.
  description: |
    LANLeecher counts download and upload per client (MAC address) for each event.

    Conventions:
    - Bytes are integers, throughput is bit/s, timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC.
    - Field names carry the direction: `bytes_down` (to the client), `bytes_up` (from the client).
      Internally `bytes_down` comes from ifHCOutOctets and `bytes_up` from ifHCInOctets of the switch port.
    - MAC addresses are accepted in any notation and returned as `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`.
    - Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.
    - Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer llk_...`. Tokens are created by admins in the web UI.
      A logged-in browser session also works; unsafe methods then need the `X-CSRF-Token` header.
  license:
    name: MIT
    identifier: MIT
servers:
  - url: /
security:
  - bearer: []
tags:
  - name: rankings
  - name: events
  - name: clients
  - name: board
  - name: operations

paths:
  /api/v1/rankings/{direction}:
    get:
      tags: [rankings]
      operationId: getRanking
      summary: Top downloaders, uploaders or total
      description: |
        Scope `read:rankings`. Hidden ports and devices are excluded unless `include_hidden=true`.
        MAC, IP and hostname fields are only included with scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - name: direction
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: string, enum: [download, upload, total]}
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/event"
        - name: limit
          in: query
          description: Number of entries (1–500). UI shortcuts are 10, 20 and 50.
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 500, default: 10}
        - name: include_hidden
          in: query
          schema: {type: boolean, default: false}
        - name: switch
          in: query
          description: Restrict to one switch (ID).
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}
        - name: from
          in: query
          description: Start of a time range (RFC 3339), uses 5-minute buckets.
          schema: {type: string, format: date-time}
        - name: to
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, format: date-time}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Ranking
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Ranking"}
              example:
                event: {name: "Basement LAN #12", slug: basement-lan-12, started_at: "2026-11-13T16:00:00Z", ended_at: null, active: true, notes: ""}
                order: download
                entries:
                  - {rank: 1, type: mac, id: 17, name: DESKTOP-FRAG42, bytes_down: 412000000000, bytes_up: 18000000000}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}
        "429": {$ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/rankings/download?limit=10"'

  /api/v1/events:
    get:
      tags: [events]
      operationId: listEvents
      summary: List events, newest first
      description: Scope `read:rankings`.
      parameters:
        - name: q
          in: query
          description: Search in name and slug.
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Events
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [events]
                properties:
                  events: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
    post:
      tags: [events]
      operationId: startEvent
      summary: Start an event (ends the running one)
      description: Scope `write:events`.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name]
              properties:
                name: {type: string, minLength: 1}
                notes: {type: string}
            example: {name: "Basement LAN #13", notes: ""}
      responses:
        "201":
          description: Started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [event]
                properties:
                  event: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}
        "403": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Forbidden"}
      x-codeSamples:
        - lang: curl
          source: |
            curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d '{"name":"Basement LAN #13"}' https://lanleecher.example/api/v1/events

  /api/v1/events/{slug}:
    get:
      tags: [events]
      operationId: getEvent
      summary: Event with totals
      description: Scope `read:rankings`.
      parameters:
        - {name: slug, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Event
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [event, totals]
                properties:
                  event: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}
                  totals: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Totals"}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}

  /api/v1/events/{slug}/stop:
    post:
      tags: [events]
      operationId: stopEvent
      summary: Stop the running event
      description: Scope `write:events`. Totals are frozen; all data stays.
      parameters:
        - {name: slug, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Stopped
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [event]
                properties:
                  event: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}
        "409": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Conflict"}

  /api/v1/clients/search:
    get:
      tags: [clients]
      operationId: searchClients
      summary: Search by MAC (any notation, partial), IP or hostname
      description: Scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - {name: q, in: query, required: true, schema: {type: string, minLength: 2}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Results
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [query, results]
                properties:
                  query: {type: string}
                  results:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      required: [device_id, name, mac, ip, hostname, last_seen, match]
                      properties:
                        device_id: {type: integer}
                        name: {type: string}
                        mac: {type: string}
                        ip: {type: string}
                        hostname: {type: string}
                        last_seen: {type: string, format: date-time}
                        match: {type: string, enum: [mac, ip, hostname]}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}

  /api/v1/clients/mac/{mac}:
    get:
      tags: [clients]
      operationId: getClient
      summary: Totals per event, IP/hostname history and ports of a MAC's device
      description: Scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/mac"
        - name: events
          in: query
          description: Only the last N events.
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Client
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Client"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}

  /api/v1/clients/mac/{mac}/timeseries:
    get:
      tags: [clients]
      operationId: getClientTimeseries
      summary: 5-minute buckets of a device in one event
      description: Scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/mac"
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/event"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Time series
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [event, bucket_seconds, points]
                properties:
                  event: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}
                  bucket_seconds: {type: integer, const: 300}
                  points:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      required: [start, bytes_down, bytes_up]
                      properties:
                        start: {type: string, format: date-time}
                        bytes_down: {type: integer}
                        bytes_up: {type: integer}
        "404": {$ref: "#/components/responses/NotFound"}

  /api/v1/clients/ip/{ip}:
    get:
      tags: [clients]
      operationId: getClientsByIP
      summary: MACs that had this IP, with time range
      description: Scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - {name: ip, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: History
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [ip, entries]
                properties:
                  ip: {type: string}
                  entries: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/History"}}

  /api/v1/clients/hostname/{name}:
    get:
      tags: [clients]
      operationId: getClientsByHostname
      summary: MACs that had this hostname (case-insensitive)
      description: Scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - {name: name, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: History
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [hostname, entries]
                properties:
                  hostname: {type: string}
                  entries: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/History"}}

  /api/v1/ports:
    get:
      tags: [clients]
      operationId: getPorts
      summary: Traffic of all ports in an event, hidden ones included
      description: Scope `read:clients`.
      parameters:
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/event"
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Ports
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [event, ports]
                properties:
                  event: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}
                  ports:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      type: object
                      required: [id, switch, if_name, label, role, hidden, bytes_down, bytes_up, unassigned_bytes_down, unassigned_bytes_up]
                      properties:
                        id: {type: integer}
                        switch: {type: string}
                        if_name: {type: string}
                        label: {type: string}
                        role: {type: string, enum: [client, multi-client, server, uplink]}
                        hidden: {type: boolean}
                        bytes_down: {type: integer}
                        bytes_up: {type: integer}
                        unassigned_bytes_down: {type: integer}
                        unassigned_bytes_up: {type: integer}

  /api/v1/board:
    get:
      tags: [board]
      operationId: getBoard
      summary: Complete beamer content
      description: |
        Scope `read:board` (or none if `board.public` is enabled). `/board` renders exactly this.
        Contains no MACs or IPs and no hidden entries. `rank_change` is positive when an entry moved up
        since the previous poll.
      security: [{bearer: []}, {}]
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, enum: [10, 20, 50], default: 10}
        - name: event
          in: query
          description: Event slug; default is the active event.
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Board
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Board"}
        "400": {$ref: "#/components/responses/BadRequest"}

  /api/v1/board/stream:
    get:
      tags: [board]
      operationId: streamBoard
      summary: Board as Server-Sent Events, one `board` event after each poll
      security: [{bearer: []}, {}]
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, enum: [10, 20, 50], default: 10}
        - name: event
          in: query
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: "Stream of `event: board` with a Board JSON in `data:`"
          content:
            text/event-stream:
              schema: {type: string}

  /api/v1/metrics:
    get:
      tags: [operations]
      operationId: getMetrics
      summary: Prometheus metrics
      description: "Scope `read:rankings`. Can be disabled with `api.metrics_enabled: false`."
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Prometheus text format
          content:
            text/plain:
              schema: {type: string}

  /health:
    get:
      tags: [operations]
      operationId: health
      summary: Liveness check without authentication
      security: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            text/plain:
              schema: {type: string, const: ok}

components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      description: "API token `llk_...` with scopes read:rankings, read:clients, write:events, read:board."
  parameters:
    event:
      name: event
      in: query
      description: Event slug, `active` (default) or `all` (rankings only).
      schema: {type: string, default: active}
    mac:
      name: mac
      in: path
      required: true
      description: MAC in any notation (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, aa-bb-..., aabb.ccdd.eeff, aabbccddeeff).
      schema: {type: string}
  responses:
    BadRequest:
      description: Invalid parameter
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or invalid token
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
    Forbidden:
      description: Missing scope, IP not allowed or CSRF failure
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
    NotFound:
      description: Unknown event, MAC or endpoint
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
    Conflict:
      description: State conflict
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
    TooManyRequests:
      description: Rate limit per token exceeded
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Problem"}
  schemas:
    Problem:
      type: object
      required: [type, title, status, code]
      properties:
        type: {type: string}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}
        code:
          type: string
          description: Stable error code.
          enum: [not_found, invalid_token, ip_not_allowed, rate_limited, csrf, unauthorized, insufficient_scope,
                 no_active_event, event_not_found, invalid_parameter, invalid_body, event_not_active, invalid_mac,
                 mac_not_found, invalid_ip, internal]
    Event:
      type: object
      required: [name, slug, started_at, ended_at, active, notes]
      properties:
        name: {type: string}
        slug: {type: string}
        started_at: {type: string, format: date-time}
        ended_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}
        active: {type: boolean}
        notes: {type: string}
    Totals:
      type: object
      required: [bytes_down, bytes_up, clients]
      properties:
        bytes_down: {type: integer}
        bytes_up: {type: integer}
        clients: {type: integer, description: Distinct MACs with credited traffic.}
    Ranking:
      type: object
      required: [event, order, entries]
      properties:
        event:
          oneOf:
            - $ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"
            - type: "null"
        order: {type: string, enum: [download, upload, total]}
        entries:
          type: array
          items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/RankingEntry"}
    RankingEntry:
      type: object
      required: [rank, type, id, name, bytes_down, bytes_up]
      properties:
        rank: {type: integer, minimum: 1}
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [mac, port_group]
          description: "`mac` is a device (one or more merged MACs); `port_group` is a port with several clients."
        id: {type: integer, description: Device ID for mac, port ID for port_group.}
        name: {type: string, description: Display name, hostname, port label or MAC.}
        bytes_down: {type: integer}
        bytes_up: {type: integer}
        hidden: {type: boolean, description: Only present with include_hidden=true.}
        mac: {type: string, description: "read:clients only"}
        macs: {type: array, items: {type: string}, description: "read:clients only"}
        ip: {type: string, description: "read:clients only"}
        hostname: {type: string, description: "read:clients only"}
    History:
      type: object
      required: [mac, value, source, first_seen, last_seen]
      properties:
        mac: {type: string}
        value: {type: string}
        source: {type: string, enum: [snmp-arp, local-neigh, dhcp, netbios, mdns, llmnr, dns-ptr]}
        first_seen: {type: string, format: date-time}
        last_seen: {type: string, format: date-time}
    Client:
      type: object
      required: [mac, device_id, name, hostname, ip, macs, hidden, events, ip_history, hostname_history, ports]
      properties:
        mac: {type: string}
        device_id: {type: integer}
        name: {type: string}
        hostname: {type: string}
        ip: {type: string}
        macs: {type: array, items: {type: string}}
        hidden: {type: boolean}
        events:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [event, bytes_down, bytes_up]
            properties:
              event: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Event"}
              bytes_down: {type: integer}
              bytes_up: {type: integer}
        ip_history: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/History"}}
        hostname_history: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/History"}}
        ports:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            required: [mac, port, vlan, first_seen, last_seen]
            properties:
              mac: {type: string}
              port: {type: string}
              vlan: {type: integer}
              first_seen: {type: string, format: date-time}
              last_seen: {type: string, format: date-time}
    Board:
      type: object
      required: [event, generated_at, totals, throughput, top_download, top_upload]
      properties:
        event:
          oneOf:
            - type: object
              required: [name, slug, started_at]
              properties:
                name: {type: string}
                slug: {type: string}
                started_at: {type: string, format: date-time}
                ended_at: {type: string, format: date-time}
            - type: "null"
        generated_at: {type: string, format: date-time}
        totals: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Totals"}
        throughput:
          type: object
          required: [down_bps, up_bps]
          properties:
            down_bps: {type: integer}
            up_bps: {type: integer}
        top_download: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/BoardEntry"}}
        top_upload: {type: array, items: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/BoardEntry"}}
    BoardEntry:
      type: object
      required: [rank, rank_change, name, type, bytes_down, bytes_up]
      properties:
        rank: {type: integer}
        rank_change: {type: integer}
        name: {type: string}
        type: {type: string, enum: [mac, port_group]}
        bytes_down: {type: integer}
        bytes_up: {type: integer}
